transcript.content: Hi, welcome in—I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. [Name]. Um, thank you so much for seeing me. I hope I'm not taking up too much of your time. 

I guess what brings me in is... well, I've just been feeling a little restless lately? It's probably nothing major, but I just feel like I can't really settle in my own body anymore. Especially when I'm supposed to sit quietly and, you know, handle paperwork or sit down with my husband to go over household plans. I just get this sort of fidgety feeling. Is that... does that make sense? I just want to make sure I'm explaining it right.
Have you started or changed the dose of any medications recently, such as antipsychotics, antidepressants, or anti-nausea drugs?

Oh, um, no. No, I haven't. I don't take any of those... I'm actually not on any prescriptions like that right now. Just, you know, a regular daily vitamin. I hope that's okay? I mean, I haven't changed anything at all recently. Is that... does that help rule things out for you?
Besides the fidgety, restless feeling, have you also been experiencing a lot of worry or anxious thoughts about different things going on in your life?

Oh, um, no, not really. I mean... I don't think so? I have the normal everyday stuff, of course, but I wouldn't say I'm excessively worried or having anxious thoughts. My life is actually really good right now, so there's not much to worry about, thankfully. 

It's really just that physical feeling of not being able to sit still, rather than my mind being anxious or stressed about things, if that makes sense? I hope I'm being clear enough. I just want to make sure I'm giving you the right information. Am I explaining that okay?
Would you say this restless, fidgety feeling is something new that started recently, or has it been a pattern you've noticed since childhood or your teenage years?

Um, well... I guess if I'm being completely honest, it's not exactly new? I mean, I don't want to make it sound like I've always been a problem or anything, but... looking back, I think this has been part of me for a really long time. Even back in elementary school. 

I was always kind of the girl who had a bit of a messy desk, or... you know, I'd forget to bring in permission slips. And my teachers, they were always so nice, but they would sometimes leave notes on my report cards saying I talked out of turn, or that I had trouble staying in my seat. I really tried my best, I promise, it just... it was hard for me to just sit there quietly. 

Does that make sense? I hope it's okay that I'm bringing up stuff from that far back. I just want to give you all the right pieces so you can figure it out. Is that the kind of thing you were looking for?
Do you currently find yourself easily distracted, losing focus during tasks, or forgetting important things at work or at home?

Um, well... I guess maybe a little bit? I mean, I try really hard to stay on task, I really do. I don't want you to think I'm just ignoring things or being lazy... but, um, sometimes if I'm trying to get something done at the kitchen table, it doesn't take much to sort of pull my attention away. 

Like, if my phone buzzes, or if I just hear a car drive by outside. Or sometimes it's just a thought, like... what I should make for dinner will pop into my head, and it just pulls me completely off track. And then, before I even notice it, I've completely stopped what I was originally doing. 

I always feel so silly when it happens, and I really do try my best to keep everything running smoothly at home. I hope that doesn't make me sound too scatterbrained? Is that... is that the kind of distraction you were asking about?
Would you say these struggles with restlessness and losing focus are causing real problems for you both at home and in other areas, like at work or in social situations?

Oh, um... well, "real problems" sounds a little... I mean, I really try not to make a big deal out of things, and I hate to complain. But... I guess, if I'm being completely honest, it has been affecting things more than I'd like to admit. 

It's mostly at home and, um, in my volunteer circles. It's really embarrassing to say this out loud, but... the fallout is that people haven't really been able to reliably count on me lately. I've actually had to step back from a few of my volunteer responsibilities because... well, I just keep letting things fall through the cracks. And I promise I'm trying so hard to stay on top of it all, I really am. I just feel awful when I let people down. 

I hope that doesn't make me sound like a terrible person? I really do want to be dependable, and I'm trying my best to fix it. Is that... does that answer your question okay?
